title: 1.1 Cauchy Problem for 1st Order Differential Equations
text:
Assume \(G\) is an open set in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n\) (or in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{C}^n\)) and \(f:G \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n\) (or \(\mathbb{C}^n\)) is a given vector field.


What does this mean?


Remark 1. 


\(G\) being an open set in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n\) (or in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{C}^n\)) means that there is a space, \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n\) (or in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{C}^n\)), that has two components:

\(\mathbb{R}\): A real-valued number that comes from the first \(\mathbb{R}\) in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n\) (or in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{C}^n\)). This is a 1-Dimensional quantity. For example, consider it as the time \(t\) dimension.
\(\mathbb{R}^n\) or \(\mathbb{C}^n\): A real-valued or complex-valued N-Dimensional vector quantity. For example, a position vector \(x\).

An example of this would be \((t, x)\), where \(t\) is from \(\mathbb{R}\) and \(x\) is from \(\mathbb{R}^n\) (or \(\mathbb{C}^n\)).
As \(G\) is an open set of \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n\) (or in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{C}^n\)), it contains points in this space but not necessarily the points along the “boundary” of the space.
The vector field by definition: a vector field is an assignment of a vector to each point in a space. Thus, \(f: G \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n\) (or \(\mathbb{C}^n\)) says that \(f\) assigns a vector in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) (or \(\mathbb{C}^n\)) to every point in \(G\).
If we think of this logical statement in relation to Newton’s equations of motion:
\[
f(t, \vec{r}) = \vec{r} = \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt}t - \frac{1}{2} \frac{d^2\vec{r}}{dt^2}t^2
\]
We see that the function \(f\) here assigns a vector, position, to each point \((t, \vec{r})\) in \(G\).


We are looking for a differentiable vector-function \[
x : \langle a,b \rangle \subset \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n \text{ (or } \mathbb{C}^n ), \ \ \  x(t) =
     \begin{pmatrix} x_1(t) \\ x_2(t) \\ \dots \\ x_n(t) \end{pmatrix} \;
\tag{1}\] which satisfies the system of \(n\) ordinary differential equations: \[
x'(t) = f(t,x(t)) \iff \begin{cases} \begin{matrix} x_1'(t) = f_1(t,x_1(t),x_2(t), \dots , x_n(t)) \\ x_2'(t) = f_1(t,x_1(t),x_2(t), \dots , x_n(t)) \\ \dots \\ x_n'(t) = f_1(t,x_1(t),x_2(t), \dots , x_n(t)) \end{matrix} \end{cases}
\tag{2}\]
In the sake of brevity we focus on the real case below. In our course we will always assume that \[
f \in C(G;\mathbb{R}^n)
\]


What does this mean?

We are looking for a differentiable vector-function that satisfies certain conditions applied on \(x\).
\(x:\langle a,b \rangle \subset \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n\), where: - \(\langle a,b \rangle\) denotes any of the intervals \((a,b)\), \([a,b]\), \([a,b)\), \((a,b]\), \([a,+\infty)\), \((-\infty,+\infty)\), etc. - \(t\) in \(x(t)\) is an element of \(\langle a,b \rangle\), a subset of \(\mathbb{R}\), and its output is a vector in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) (or \(\mathbb{C}^n\)) with \(n\) components.
This vector-function satisfies the system of \(n\) ordinary differential equations:
\[
x'(t) = f(t, x(t)) \iff
\begin{cases}
x_1'(t) = f_1(t, x_1(t), x_2(t), \dots, x_n(t)) \\
x_2'(t) = f_2(t, x_1(t), x_2(t), \dots, x_n(t)) \\
\vdots \\
x_n'(t) = f_n(t, x_1(t), x_2(t), \dots, x_n(t))
\end{cases} \ \ \ \ \ \ \ (2)
\]
This defines another condition applied to \(x\): the derivative of \(x\) is a function \(f\) that maps the inputs \(t\) and \(x(t)\) to another vector:
\[
f(t, x(t)) =
\begin{pmatrix}
f_1(t, x_1(t), x_2(t), \dots, x_n(t)) \\
f_2(t, x_1(t), x_2(t), \dots, x_n(t)) \\
\vdots \\
f_n(t, x_1(t), x_2(t), \dots, x_n(t))
\end{pmatrix} = x'(t)
\]
Note here that \(f(t, x(t)) = x'(t)\) makes \(x(t)\) a differentiable function. Furthermore, the condition that this differential function must be an Ordinary Differential Equation is placed on \(f(t, x(t)) = x'(t)\).
Finally, \(f \in C(G; \mathbb{R}^n)\) states that the function \(f\) is continuous and nice.

title: 1.1 Cauchy Problem for 1st Order Differential Equations
text:
2. Definition of a solution
\(D\tiny{EFINITION}\). We say that \(x:\langle a,b \rangle \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n\) is a solution to the system Equation 2 iff

\(x \in C^1(\langle a,b \rangle;\mathbb{R}^n)\)
\((t,x(t)) \in G, \ \ \ \forall t \in \langle a,b \rangle\)
\(x'(t) = f(t,x(t)), \ \ \ \forall t \in \langle a,b \rangle\)



What does this mean?

This point simply states that a differentiable vector-function \(x\) is a solution to the system of \(n\) ordinary differential equation, Equation 2, if and only if:

\(x\), with \(n\) components, is continuously differentiable across the interval \(\langle a, b \rangle\).
For all \(t\) that is an element in the interval \(\langle a, b \rangle\), \(t\) and \(x(t)\) are an element of \(G\).

Remember: \(G\) is an open set in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n\) (or in \(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{C}^n\)).

For all \(t\) that is an element in the interval \(\langle a, b \rangle\), the derivative of \(x(t)\), \(x'(t)\), is equal to the function \(f(t, x(t))\).
This condition seems trivial since \(f(t, x(t))\) is defined by \(f(t, x(t)) = x'(t)\). However, it also places the restriction on \(x(t)\) that it must be a function.

title: 1.1 Cauchy Problem for 1st Order Differential Equations
text:
3. Cauchy Problem
We will also consider the Cauchy Problem for the system (\(2\)): for given \(x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^n\) and \(t_0 \in \langle a,b \rangle\) such that \((t_0,x_0) \in G\) for a solution \(x \in C^1(\langle a,b \rangle;\mathbb{R}^n)\) of the system, Equation 2 , such that: \[
\begin{cases} \begin{matrix} x'(t) = f(t,x(t)), \ \ \ \ t\in \langle a,b\rangle \\ x(t_0) = x_0 \end{matrix} \end{cases}
\tag{3}\]


What does this mean?

The most difficult part of this point is the term Cauchy Problem perhaps its easier to think of it as it’s other, more popular name The Initial Value Problem. where there is some initial value \(x(t_0) = x_0\) with \(t_0\) an element of an arbitrary interval \(\langle a,b \rangle\) such that the “point” \((t_0,x_0)\) is an element of \(G\) Remark 1.

for a solution \(x \in C^1(\langle a,b \rangle;\mathbb{R}^n)\) of the system (2)

for a solution \(x\) which is a function that is continuously differentiable along the arbitary domain \(\langle a,b \rangle\) such that it is in \(\mathbb{R}^n\). recall that \(x\) here references the function, Equation 1 , previously defined and . more conditions on \(x\) are then applied \(x'(t) = f(t,x(t)), \ \ \ t\in \langle a,b \rangle\) and \(x(t_0)=x_0\). if we compare these conditions with Equation 2 we see that the solution the Cauchy Problem Initial Value Problem has the derivative \(x'(t)\) that is equal to Equation 2.

title: 1.1 Cauchy Problem for 1st Order Differential Equations
section: 4. Reduction of the Cauchy problem to the integral equation
text:
4. Reduction of the Cauchy problem to the integral equation
\(T\tiny{HEOREM}\) Assume \(x_0 \in \mathbb{R}^n\) and \(t_0 \in \langle a,b \rangle\) satisfy \((t_0,x_0) \in G\). A function \(x : \langle a,b \rangle \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^n\) is a solution to the Cauchy problem, Equation 3, if and only if:

\(x \in C(\langle a,b \rangle;\mathbb{R}^n)\)
\((t,x(t)) \in G, \ \ \ \forall t \in \langle a,b \rangle\)
The function \(x(t)\) satisfies the integral equation

\[x(t) = x_0 + \int_{t_0}^tf(\tau,x(\tau)) \ d\tau , \ \ \ \forall t \in \langle a,b \rangle\]


What does this mean?

Points 1 and 2 have been covered before, a quick recap is: \(x\) is continuous along the arbitary interval \(\langle a,b \rangle\) such that it is in \(\mathbb{R}^n\). and the “point”\((t,x(t))\) is a subset of \(G\), Remark 1, for \(t\) along the arbitary interval \(\langle a,b \rangle\).
The third point applies the condition on \(x(t)\) such it is equal to the integral of \(f(t,x(t))\), Equation 2, from \(t_0\) to \(t\), and has been parametrized by \(\tau\) where \(t\) is in the arbitary interval \(\langle a,b \rangle\).

title: 1.1 Cauchy Problem for 1st Order Differential Equations
text:
5. Peano’s interval
Assume \((t_0,x_0) \in G\) and \(r >0\) and \(R>0\) satisfy: \[
\bar{P}_{r,R}(t_0,x_0) := [t_0 - r,t_0+r] \times \bar{B}_R(x_0) \subset G
\] As \(\bar{P}_{r,R}(t_0,x_0)\) is compact and \(f \in C(\bar{P}_{r,R}(t_0,x_0))\) we can define \[
M:=\sup\limits_{(t,x)\in \bar{P}_{r,R}(t_0,x_0)} |f(t,x)|.
\] Introduce a positive number \[
h := \min \left\{ {r,\frac{R}{M}}\right\}
\]
Then the interval \([t_0-h,t_0+h]\) is called the Peano Interval for \(f\) and \(\bar{P}_{r,R}(t_0,x_0)\).
\(T\tiny{HEOREM}.\) If \(x(t)\) is a solution to the Cauchy problem, Equation 3, and \([t_0 - h,t_0+h]\) we have \(x(t) \in B_R(x_0)\).

title: 1.1 Cauchy Problem for 1st Order Differential Equations
text:
6. Euler method
Assume \(P_{r,R}(t_0,x_0) \subset G\) and let \([t_0-h, t_0+h]\) be the Peano interval for \(f\) and \(\bar{P}_{r,R}(t_0,x_0)\). For any \(m \in \mathbb{N}\) we split the interval \([t_0,h]\) into \(m\) parts by points \[
t_0 < t_1 < t_2 < \ ... \ < t_m = t_0 + h, \ \ \ \ \ t_k=t_0+\frac{k}{m}h, \ \  k = 0,1,...,m
\]
then we define points \({\{x_k\} }_{k=1}^{m} \subset \mathbb{R}^n\) recursively as solutions of the following equation:
\[
\frac{x_k - x_{k-1}}{t_k - t_{k-1}} = f(t_{k-1},x_{}k-1), \ \ \ \ k=1,2,...,m, \ \ \ \ t_k - t_{k-1}=\frac{h}{m}.
\] In other words, we define points, \(x_1,x_2,...,x_m\) in the following recursive way: \[
x_1 = x_0 + f(t_0,x_0)\frac{h}{m}, \ \ \ x_2 = x_1 + f(t_1,x_1)\frac{h}{m}, \ \ \ ... \ \ \ x_m = x_{m-1} + f(t_{m-1},x_{m})\frac{h}{m}.
\] Then for any \(t \in [t_0,h]\) we define the forward Euler approximations \(\varphi_m(t)\) for the Cauchy problem, Equation 3, as a piece-wise linear continuous function: \[
\varphi_m(t) := x_{k-1} + \frac{x_k - x_{k-1}}{t_k - t_{k-1}}(t-t_{k-1}),
\ \ \ \ \forall t \in [t_{k-1},t_k], \ \ \ \ k=1,2,...,m
\] similar we can define the backward Euler approximations \(\varphi_m(t)\) on the interval \([t_0 - h, t_0]\).

title: 1.1 Cauchy Problem for 1st Order Differential Equations
text:
7. Compactness of Euler approximations
\(T\tiny{HEOREM}.\) Assume \(\bar{P}_{r,R}(t_0,x_0) \subset G\) and let \([t_0-h,t_0+h]\) be the Peano interval for \(f\) and \(\bar{P}_{r,R}(t_0,x_0)\). Assume \(\varepsilon_m \rightarrow +0\).
Then for any \(m \in \mathbb{N}\) there exists \(N=N(m) \in \mathbb{N}\) such that the EUler approximations \(\varphi_m \in C([t_0 - h,t_0+h];\mathbb{R}^n)\) for the Cauchy problem, Equation 3, (corresponding to the mesh of partition \(\frac{h}{}\)) possess the following properties:

\(\varphi_m(t) \in \bar{B}_R(x_0) , \ \ \ \ \forall t \subset [t_0 - h, t_0 + h]\)
\(|\varphi_m'(t) - f(t,\varphi_m(t))| \le \varepsilon_m , \ \ \ \ \forall t \in [t_0 - h, t_0 + h]\)
functions \(\{ \varphi_m \}_{m=1}^{\infty}\) are uniformly bounded on \([t_0 - h, t_0 + h]\)
functions \(\{ \varphi_m \}_{m=1}^{\infty}\) are uniformly equicontinuous on \([t_0 - h, t_0 + h]\)

title: Personal Financial Reports
text:
The Features of this project are as follows:

Uses CSV files from Online Banking Portals
Supports Multiple Accounts and Accounts from different Banks
Naming and Tagging of Transactions

i.e. Tags and Naming for transactions such as:

Vendor: Aldi
Major: Food
Minor: Groceries


Constructs Tables and Graphs from Account Data
Outputs a PDF monthly financial report with Tables and Graphs

To approach this project I have broken it down into 4 parts:

Import and Process Raw Data into ‘processed files’ and save them
append unique transaction data from the processed csv files to a collated master CSV file
Processing the master CSV data
Creating Figures from master CSV file
Generating a PDF file and populating with Figures.

section: Part 1: Handling Raw Data and Formatting to Processed Data
text:
Part 1: Handling Raw Data and Formatting to Processed Data
The transaction data is obtained from the export feature available from most online banking portals. This data first needs to imported and parse.
def ProcessRaw():
    for i in raw_data_files:
        if list(i)[0] == ".": #I am on mac so this avoids .DS_Store
            continue
        print(f"Processing {i}")
        raw_file_path = os.path.join(raw_data_folder,i)
        processed_filepath = os.path.join(processed_data_folder,i)  
        if Banks["FirstBank"] in i:
            df = pd.read_csv(raw_file_path,delimiter=";")
            DataFormatBankOne(df)
            DropColumnsBankOne(df)
            df = ReorderBankOne(df)
            df = ReorderBankOne(df)
            CreateMainID(df) # Needed for avoiding duplicate transactions
            SaveProcessed(df,processed_filepath)
        if Banks["Commbank"] in i:
            df = pd.read_csv(raw_file_path,delimiter=";")
            # Similar Formatting to First Bank
            CreateMainID(df)
            SaveProcessed(df,processed_filepath)
        print(f"Processed {i} saved to {processed_filepath}\n")
the Banks Dictionary is a dictionary with keys as the name of the bank/account, and its values consist of some regex within its filename to identify as different banks/account have different headers and data formats, dates in particular. e.g.
Banks = {"Sparkasse":"sparkasse.*", # filename contains sparkasse
        "Deutsche Bank":"^DB.*" # filename starts with DB
        }  
The ProcessRaw() function iterates through all files in raw_data_files and based on the identified bank/account a series of formatting functions are performed to standarized the data, and concluding with the CreateMainID() function.
def CreateMainIDSparkasse(df):
    """
    A Simple Hash to create a discernible primary key across data files.
    """
    df["ID"] = (pd.util
    .hash_pandas_object(df[["Confirmaton date", "Amount", "Vendor"]]
    ,index=False).abs())
    return None
This function solves a lack of a unified primary key, as well as discerning duplicate transactions for the case where the same transaction exists in multiple files, that will be modified by using a combination of data columns that will not be altered to create a simple, unique hash value.
For my case this happended frequently as two of my csv files had the largely the same data as a result of exporting the last year of data twice, two months apart.
The formatting functions DataFormatBankOne,DropColumnsBankOne and ReorderBankOne are largely dependant on your transaction data and as such I won’t show the functions here. The goal of these functions is to format each banks transaction data to the same data formats and column headers e.g.
Dropcolumns example
The use of
if Banks["FirstBank"] in i:
# and
if Banks["SecondBank"] in i:
could be replace with something like
for key in Bank:
    df = pd.read_csv(raw_file_path,delimiter=";")
    DataFormatBankOne(df,key)
    DropColumnsBankOne(df,key)
    df = ReorderBankOne(df,key)
    df = RenameBankOne(df,key)
    CreateMainID(df)
    SaveProcessed(df,processed_filepath)
for a large amount of banks/accounts and passing the Bank key into the formatting functions to handle differences. I was only working with two banks so I saw no need to make things more complicated.
Thus ProcessRaw() imports the raw data and formats the pandas dataframes into a standardized set of columns and data formats. It then saves this dataframe as a csv into a processed folder with the rest of the processed dataframes for merging into the master CSV file.
def SaveProcessed(df,processed_filepath):
    if os.path.exists(processed_filepath):
        os.remove(processed_filepath)
    df.to_csv(processed_filepath,sep=";",index=False)
    return None

title: Personal Financial Reports
section: Parts 2 and 3: Processing and Collating Master CSV
text:
Parts 2 and 3: Processing and Collating Master CSV
For simplicity it was decided to merge parts 2 and 3. This results in a single for loop that first imports the processed csv data into a dataframe, creates all tags and any additional formatting steps to that dataframe, and finally appends only new data rows to the master CSV based on the ID Hash previously created:
mf = isMasterdata() # Safe import csv File
processed_data_files = csvFiles(processed_data_folder)
Vendor_Dict = ImportVendorListFromIni(Vendor_path)
for file in processed_data_files:
    bf=pd.read_csv(file,delimiter=";")
    if Banks["FirstBank"] in file:
        bf = ApplyVendorList(df,Vendor_Dict)
        bf = BankOneMasterFormat(df)
        bf = ClassifyVarious(df) 
        #^ Various classifcations that are not suitable for ApplyVendorList()
        bf = ApplyTags(df,Tags_path)
        bf = ImportAndApplyRecurrings(df,Recurs_path) 
        #^ Classify Recurring payments based on a list
    new_rows = df[~df["ID"].isin(mf["ID"])]
    if Banks["SecondBank"] in file:
        bf = ApplyVendorList(df,Vendor_Dict)
        bf = BankTwoMasterFormat(df)
        bf = ClassifyVarious(df) 
        #^ Various classifcations that are not suitable for ApplyVendorList()
        bf = ApplyTags(df,Tags_path)
        bf = ImportAndApplyRecurrings(df,Recurs_path) 
        #^ Classify Recurring payments based on a list
    new_rows = bf[~bf["ID"].isin(mf["ID"])]
    if mf.empty: # --
        mf = new_rows.copy() # -- Avoids a FutureWarning
    elif not new_rows.empty:  # --
        mf = pd.concat([mf, new_rows], ignore_index=True) 
        #^ Only add if unique ID

ExportMFtoMasterTransactions(mf,mastercsv_filePath)
Explaining the above code cell, the first function isMasterdata(), first checks if the Master CSV File exists, if it does it, outputs a dataframe of the csv. If it doesnt exists it creates the file and populates it with the column headings, then outputs the mf dataframe.
def isMasterdata():
    masterCols = ["ID","Vendor","Cost","Currency","Data","Comment"
    ,"Account","AccountNo.","BIC (SWIFT-Code)","Un/Necessary",
    "Major","Minor","IsReccuring"]
    if os.path.exists(mastercsv_filePath):
        mf = pd.read_csv(mastercsv_filePath,delimiter=";")
    else:
        f = open(mastercsv_filePath,"a")
        strCols = ''
        for i in masterCols:
            strCols = strCols + ";" + i
        f.write(strCols[1:])
        f.close()
        mf = pd.read_csv(mastercsv_filePath,delimiter=";")
    return mf
I will skip over ImportVendorListFromIni() as thats self-explanatory, and once again the functions ApplyVendorList(), BankMasterFormat(),… are dependent on the formatting of your csv files, as well as your preferences for the tags you want to create from your data and ultimately what you will want to keep track of in terms of your personal finances. One such tag I recommend is indicating which payments are regularly recurring.
Once the bank dataframe bf is formatted and ready to be merged, the first step is find the new rows in bf that are not in mf
new_rows = bf[~bf["ID"].isin(mf["ID"])] # a dataframe of only new rows
With that dataframe we want to add those rows to mf. If mf is empty, (This happens when the masterCSV does not exist and is created in isMasterdata()), we can simply overwrite mf with a copy of new_rows
if mf.empty:
        mf = new_rows.copy()
If mf is not empty we concatenate the new_rows dataframe to the end of mf.
elif not new_rows.empty:
        mf = pd.concat([mf, new_rows], ignore_index=True) 
        #^ Only add if unique ID
If your column headers in new_rows are not the same as in mf pd.concat() will create unwanted column headers in your mf. I would advise making the bf columns headers the same as mf in your formatting section of the for loop.
Finally mf is safely exported to the master CSV file with ExportMFtoMasterTransactions()

section: Part 4: Creating Figures from Master CSV File
text:
Part 4: Creating Figures from Master CSV File
With Formatting the data completed, now figures, tables and graphs can be created to visualize monthly spending, spending categories, and more. As too what figures to create that is dependent on what you want to track, aspects of your finances you want to monitor.
E.g. if you want to monitor your savings progress each month, you can create a table of your income, expenses, net and savings ratio

Example Overview Table

For a graph, a breakdown of your Monthly purchases based on Major and Minor categories can be useful, for example:





As for what went with, for this project I had the following figures, creating using pandas,plotly and IPython for the previous month.

Overview Table: Income, Expenses and Net
Expenses Table: Breaks down expenses based on Major and Minor tags
Necessities Table: Outlines and totals expenses that are deemed necessary
Recurring Payments Table: Outlines and totals expenses that are recurring and nex payment data
Majors Pie Chart: Pie chart of expenses based on Major Tags
Neccessaries and Unneccessaries Pie Chart: Visualizes percentage of necessary and unnecessary expenses that month.

The full code for these figures can be found on github at: https://github.com/Jordoler/FinReports in CreateFigures.py

title: Personal Financial Reports
text:
Part 5: Generating the Report

Foreword
To generate the report, lots of different methods and modules were tried, originally the idea was to create a juypter notebook and use nbconvert however the styling options were limited. ReportLab was investigated, however provded too complex and complicated for the project.
Finally a mutli-step pdf generation method was chosen that utilises Quarto to generate a stylized html page of the report, and playwright to save this html page as a pdf, using a headless chromium browser.
The key benefit with this approach is that I have experience using Quarto and thus know how to easily style the report to my liking, additionally Playwright browser.new_page().pdf() function maintains alot of the geometry and styling of the Quarto html page.






Note



This website was created using Quarto!


I focused on creating a template with Quarto that I can then populate create month’s financial report with, this proved rather confusing as Quarto’s documentation mentions support for variables via a _variables.yml and using {{< var VARIABLE_NAME >}} in the .qmd file, more info here although this didn’t seem to work, so I opted for using the integrated notebook feature in Quarto to display graphs and tables.
